body_es: OpenAPI (anteriormente Swagger) es un estándar para documentar APIs REST. FastAPI genera automáticamente especificaciones OpenAPI basadas en los tipos de datos de las rutas. La documentación interactiva está disponible en /docs (Swagger UI) y /redoc (ReDoc). Se pueden agregar descripciones detalladas, ejemplos, y códigos de respuesta usando docstrings y configuración. Las pruebas pueden escribirse con pytest y verificar códigos de estado, estructura de respuesta, y comportamiento. Una documentación clara y pruebas exhaustivas son esenciales para APIs mantenibles.
body_en: OpenAPI (formerly Swagger) is a standard for documenting REST APIs. FastAPI automatically generates OpenAPI specifications based on route data types. Interactive documentation is available at /docs (Swagger UI) and /redoc (ReDoc). Detailed descriptions, examples, and response codes can be added using docstrings and configuration. Tests can be written with pytest and verify status codes, response structure, and behavior. Clear documentation and comprehensive tests are essential for maintainable APIs.
example_code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List

app = FastAPI(
    title="User API",
    description="API for managing users",
    version="1.0.0"
)

class User(BaseModel):
    """User model"""
    id: int = Field(..., description="Unique user identifier")
    name: str = Field(..., description="User full name", min_length=1)
    email: str = Field(..., description="User email address")
    age: int = Field(None, description="User age", ge=0, le=150)

class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    """User creation request"""
    name: str = Field(..., description="User full name")
    email: str = Field(..., description="User email")
    age: int = Field(None, description="User age")

@app.get("/users", response_model=List[User], tags=["users"])
async def list_users(
    skip: int = Field(0, description="Number of records to skip"),
    limit: int = Field(10, description="Maximum records to return")
):
    """List all users with pagination.
    
    - **skip**: Number of users to skip (default 0)
    - **limit**: Maximum users to return (default 10)
    """
    return [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com", "age": 30}]

@app.post("/users", response_model=User, status_code=201, tags=["users"])
async def create_user(user: UserCreate):
    """Create a new user.
    
    Returns:
        User: The newly created user with assigned ID
    """
    return {"id": 1, **user.dict()}

@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=User, tags=["users"])
async def get_user(user_id: int = Field(..., description="User ID")):
    """Get a specific user by ID.
    
    Args:
        user_id: The unique identifier of the user
    """
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com", "age": 30}

# Testing with pytest
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_list_users():
    response = client.get("/users")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert isinstance(data, list)
    assert len(data) > 0
    assert "id" in data[0]

def test_create_user():
    user_data = {"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com", "age": 25}
    response = client.post("/users", json=user_data)
    assert response.status_code == 201
    data = response.json()
    assert data["name"] == "Bob"
    assert data["email"] == "bob@example.com"

def test_get_user():
    response = client.get("/users/1")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert data["id"] == 1
    assert "name" in data

def test_get_nonexistent_user():
    response = client.get("/users/99999")
    assert response.status_code == 404
